steps.title: Import TypeScript utilities for type safety
steps.instruction: Import the TypeScript utilities needed for building a typed query key factory. Import the 'QueryKey' type from '@tanstack/react-query'.
steps.hint: You'll need to import the QueryKey type from the react-query library to ensure type safety for your query keys.
steps.analogousExample:
// Similar: importing a type from a library
import { ComponentProps } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: The QueryKey type is imported, providing the foundation for type-safe query keys.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've imported the QueryKey type, which is essential for building type-safe query keys.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing QueryKey from '@tanstack/react-query'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The import statement is missing or incorrect. You need to import QueryKey from '@tanstack/react-query'.

steps.title: Define the base query key type structure
steps.instruction: Define a TypeScript type called QueryKeyStructure that represents the base structure of a query key. It should be an object type with a 'scope' property of type string and a 'params' property of type Record<string, unknown>.
steps.hint: Use the 'type' keyword to create a type alias. The 'Record<string, unknown>' type represents an object with string keys and any values.
steps.seedCode:
// Import the QueryKey type from '@tanstack/react-query'

// Define your QueryKeyStructure type here
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have a TypeScript type that serves as the foundation for your typed query key factory.
successCriteria: A QueryKeyStructure type is defined with 'scope' (string) and 'params' (Record<string, unknown>) properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the base type structure for query keys. This will ensure type safety throughout your query key factory.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your type has both 'scope' and 'params' properties with the correct types.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't match what we need. Remember to create a type with 'scope' as string and 'params' as Record<string, unknown>.

steps.title: Create the query key factory function signature
steps.instruction: Declare a function named createQueryKeyFactory with a generic type parameter T that extends QueryKeyStructure. The function should take a single argument 'base' of type T and return a typed query key factory.
steps.hint: Use a function declaration or arrow function with proper TypeScript generics: <T extends QueryKeyStructure>.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function signature for createQueryKeyFactory with proper generic typing is added to the code.
successCriteria: The createQueryKeyFactory function is declared with a generic type parameter T extending QueryKeyStructure, takes a 'base' argument of type T, and returns a typed factory.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've correctly declared the query key factory function signature with proper TypeScript generics.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure your function has a generic type parameter <T extends QueryKeyStructure> and takes a 'base' argument of type T.
steps.feedbackWrong: The function signature is missing or incorrect. It should be a generic function that accepts a typed 'base' parameter.

steps.title: Implement the factory function body
steps.instruction: Inside the createQueryKeyFactory function, implement the function body to return a nested object structure that matches your QueryKeyStructure type.
steps.hint: The function should return an object where each key is a function that returns a query key array. For example, for a 'users' key, you might have users: () => ['users'].
steps.expectedOutcome: The createQueryKeyFactory function now has a complete implementation that returns an object matching the QueryKeyStructure type.
successCriteria: The createQueryKeyFactory function returns an object with at least one key that is a function returning a query key array.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented the factory function body. The function now returns a structured object that will serve as your typed query key factory.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the function returns an object with functions that return query key arrays. Check that your implementation matches the QueryKeyStructure type you defined earlier.
steps.feedbackWrong: The implementation doesn't match what's needed. Remember, createQueryKeyFactory should return an object where each property is a function that returns a query key array. Review the QueryKeyStructure type you defined.

steps.title: Add type parameters for flexibility
steps.instruction: Add a generic type parameter T to the createQueryKeyFactory function signature to make it accept different data types.
steps.hint: Add <T> after the function name, before the parentheses, to declare a generic type parameter.
steps.expectedOutcome: The createQueryKeyFactory function should now have a generic type parameter <T> in its signature.
successCriteria: The function signature includes a generic type parameter <T>.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! Adding the generic type parameter makes your factory flexible to work with different data types.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you added the generic type parameter <T> directly after the function name.
steps.feedbackWrong: The generic type parameter is missing. Add <T> after the function name to declare it.

steps.title: Create helper types for query key composition
steps.instruction: Define a new type named QueryKeyHelper that extends the QueryKeyStructure type to include a 'compose' method signature.
steps.hint: Use the 'type' keyword to create QueryKeyHelper as an interface-like type that extends QueryKeyStructure and adds a compose method.
steps.expectedOutcome: A QueryKeyHelper type is defined that extends QueryKeyStructure and includes a compose method signature for building complex query keys.
successCriteria: QueryKeyHelper type is defined with proper extension syntax and includes a compose method signature.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully defined the QueryKeyHelper type with composition capabilities.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've defined a type, but check that it properly extends QueryKeyStructure and includes the compose method signature.
steps.feedbackWrong: The QueryKeyHelper type definition is missing or incorrect. Make sure it extends QueryKeyStructure and includes a compose method.

steps.title: Add validation for query key arguments
steps.instruction: Inside your createQueryKeyFactory function, add a validation check at the beginning of the function body to ensure the base argument is a string.
steps.hint: You can add a simple runtime check using typeof and throw an error if the condition fails.
steps.expectedOutcome: The createQueryKeyFactory function now includes runtime validation for its base argument.
successCriteria: The function contains a typeof check that throws an error when the base argument is not a string.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added proper validation to ensure type safety at runtime boundaries.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're checking that the base argument is a string and throwing an appropriate error.
steps.feedbackWrong: The validation logic is missing or incorrect. Add a check using typeof to validate the base argument type.

steps.title: Export the factory and types
steps.instruction: Export the createQueryKeyFactory function and the QueryKeyStructure type using named exports.
steps.hint: Use the 'export' keyword before the function and type declarations to make them available for import in other files.
steps.expectedOutcome: The createQueryKeyFactory function and QueryKeyStructure type are exported and ready to be used in other modules.
successCriteria: Both createQueryKeyFactory and QueryKeyStructure are exported as named exports.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully exported the factory and type, making them available for use throughout your application.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've exported one item, but remember to export both the createQueryKeyFactory function and QueryKeyStructure type.
steps.feedbackWrong: The exports are missing or incorrect. Use named exports to make both the function and type available outside this module.

steps.title: Create example usage of the factory
steps.instruction: Create an example function named 'exampleUsage' that demonstrates how to use the typed query key factory.
steps.hint: Define a function that calls createQueryKeyFactory and uses its methods to create and extend query keys.
steps.expectedOutcome: A function named 'exampleUsage' is created that demonstrates practical use of the query key factory.
successCriteria: The 'exampleUsage' function is defined, calls createQueryKeyFactory, and uses its create and/or extend methods.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created an example that shows how the typed query key factory can be used in practice.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the example, but make sure to include calls to the factory methods like create or extend to fully demonstrate usage.
steps.feedbackWrong: The example function isn't quite right. Remember to create a function named 'exampleUsage' that uses the query key factory methods.

steps.title: Test the factory with different scenarios
steps.instruction: Create a test function named testQueryKeyFactory that validates the factory works with different input scenarios.
steps.hint: Define a function that calls createQueryKeyFactory with different arguments and logs or returns the results.
steps.expectedOutcome: A test function is created that can validate the factory's type safety and functionality with various inputs.
successCriteria: The testQueryKeyFactory function is defined and contains test scenarios for the query key factory.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've created a test function to validate the factory's behavior with different scenarios.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the test function, but make sure it includes test scenarios for the factory.
steps.feedbackWrong: The test function isn't properly defined. Create a function named testQueryKeyFactory that tests the factory.
